transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-10-13
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~47 minutes
- Attendees: Jamie Ortega (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Morris (Cedarwood CTO), Diego Alvarez (SRE), Priya Singh (ML Eng)

Summary: quick discovery; Cedarwood evaluating exit from OpenAI and run some workloads on a private/Dedicated hosting option. Main concerns: eval parity with current OpenAI models, vLLM/TGI compatibility, latency and cost tradeoffs, security (KMS, SSO), and benchmark plan.

Topics: migration path, model parity, Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC), quantization/throughput, KV cache and prefix caching, canary rollouts, audit logs and SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML integration, fallback policies.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jamie: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we've got about 45 minutes, i'm jamie with redwood inference, joining is samir, our solutions engineer. can you do quick intros?
[00:08] Lena: sure, lena, cto at cedarwood, we own a bunch of customer facing conversational flows, currently mostly on OpenAI and a few finetuned endpoints with Anthropic for safety checks.
[00:18] Diego: diego, infra, i run our k8s and the vpc stuff, i'll care about networking and keys.
[00:22] Priya: priya, ml eng, i own model serving and evals.
[00:26] Samir: great, thanks. quick background from redwood: we offer hosted api, dedicated reserved capacity and private vpc/on-prem installs — same api surface but different hosting and security options — latency and cost knobs vary, and we've got tooling for rollouts and evals.
[00:40] Lena: high level, we're moving off OpenAI because of pricing and audit concerns, also want more control over data. key questions: can you run our current prompt sets with parity? what about vllm or TGI compatibility, and how disruptive is the migration?
[00:52] Jamie: good Q. Samir, wanna take parity/compatibility?
[00:54] Samir: yeah. short answer: we aim for eval parity but it depends on exact model and decoding params. we have a model catalog, we onboard a matching open model or quantized variant, and run evals against your prompt suites. sometimes tokenization or sampling differences cause drift, esp with top-p/temp combos, but we have guardrails — eval harness, reranking, and small finetune/retemping if needed.
[01:20] Priya: when you say model catalog, do you host the same checkpoint from openai or is it an open substitute?
[01:26] Samir: in most cases it's an open checkpoint equivalent — so not the proprietary openai weights — we try to match behavior with curated model choices. for customers needing exact deterministic parity we recommend a dedicated eval period; sometimes a light finetune on your prompt set gets you there.
[01:40] Diego: network question: for private, do we bring our own k8s or is it redwood-managed? and how does kms work?
[01:47] Jamie: private gives you a customer-managed VPC and control plane; you can run the inference nodes in your account or on-prem. KMS is supported via customer key injection — we integrate with AWS KMS or bring-your-own HSM patterns.
[02:00] Diego: ok, that's important. Compliance team will want logs and audit trail retention.
[02:04] Samir: we emit audit logs and token-level traces in the console, retention tiers are configurable; for enterprise we also stream logs to your SIEM via syslog or S3.
[02:12] Lena: another one: runway. timeline is tight — we'd like to switch traffic in q1 2027 but start a POC this quarter. what's typical for a migration?
[02:20] Jamie: POC is usually 4-6 weeks: discovery, small benchmark, parity eval, then pilot on a subset of traffic. for Dedicated reserved capacity we can fast-track a week-long trial for benchmarks.
[02:32] Priya: benchmarks — we have a mix of short chat prompts and long doc summarization, token lengths average 250 with tails to 2k. how do you manage kv cache and batching?
[02:44] Samir: runtime handles kv cache for streams; we do prefix caching for repeated contexts and smart batching — configurable batch windows per SLO. for long sequences we switch kernels and can enable quantization friendly paths. that saves tokens and GPU time.
[03:02] Diego: any gotchas moving from vLLM in-house to your runtime? we currently use vllm with some custom hooks.
[03:09] Samir: two things — we have a vllm compatibility layer for common envs and support TGI-style endpoints, but custom hooks/plugins may need porting. if you rely on vllm's callback internals that's the main migration work. we can run a smoke test using your vllm config to find gaps.
[03:26] Priya: what about quantization? we run int8 and bfloat16 in places. does redwood support quantized variants and mixed precision?
[03:33] Samir: yes, the serving runtime supports several quantization profiles — int8, nf4-like, and mixed precision on compatible hw. we also do kernel selection — sometimes int8 reduces perf on accuracy-sensitive tasks so we'll recommend per-model profiles based on your evals.
[03:48] Lena: cost question — compare hosted vs dedicated vs private. we'd like predictable costs and control but not manage everything.
[03:56] Jamie: hosted is per-token variable pricing with quick onboarding. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with monthly commit — very predictable and lower per-token cost at scale. Private (VPC) has platform fees plus infra costs you manage — best for strict compliance. we can send a cost model with your usage profile.
[04:16] Diego: SLA — do you offer latency SLOs on Dedicated?
[04:19] Samir: yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed latency and uptime tiers; for private it depends on the customer's infra but we provide runbooks for SLO targets.
[04:28] Priya: eval parity again — can you run A/B with our prod traffic? we need side-by-side scoring and drift metrics.
[04:35] Samir: absolutely, we support shadowing/side-by-side A/B and have builtin eval dashboards — you can compare outputs, token usage, and quality metrics; also regression alerts tied to prompt sets.
[04:47] Lena: security: SSO and RBAC, SAML, SCIM, compliance artifacts — can you integrate with our identity provider?
[04:55] Jamie: yes, SSO (SAML/OIDC) and SCIM for provisioning, RBAC and token scoping are supported. for enterprise we do an onboarding checklist with your sec team.
[05:05] Diego: any references for customers who moved off OpenAI successfully?
[05:08] Jamie: we've got case studies and a couple of retailer references; i'll share redacted logs and a migration playbook.
[05:16] Priya: curious about fallback policies — if a Dedicated model is saturated do you fallback to hosted? how transparent is that?
[05:23] Samir: smart routing supports policy-based fallback — you can set region, tier, cost vs latency priorities. fallbacks can go to compatible model variants or hosted pool; it's visible in console and tracing.
[05:34] Lena: what's your approach to sensitive PII data — do you recommend token scrubbing at edge or bring to redwood?
[05:41] Samir: we recommend edge scrubbing when possible; for Private deployments data never leaves your VPC. For Hosted we offer data controls and can PII-redact at ingress; encryption in transit and at rest with customer KMS keys.
[05:55] Priya: for the POC, we want to validate two things: perf parity for our top-50 prompts and a cost delta for 6 months of traffic. can you support that?
[06:03] Jamie: yes — typical POC scope. we'll run the parity eval and a cost analysis. Samir will own benchmarks.
[06:09] Diego: network and egress — will traffic to model replicas within our vpc count as egress between accounts? need to check with finance.
[06:17] Jamie: depends on hosting option; for Dedicated in our cloud it's within same provider, for Private in your account it's internal. we'll add egress notes in the cost doc.
[06:25] Priya: one more — how do you handle model updates and rollouts?
[06:29] Samir: rollouts support canaries and A/B, automatic fallback if latency increases or error rate spikes. we keep model version pinning so you can pin a route to a version and gradually shift traffic.
[06:41] Lena: any time we might need finetune help or retraining? we don't want to own that initially.
[06:46] Jamie: we offer professional services around finetune and prompt-engineering for an engagement fee, or you can use our eval harness to self-run.
[06:55] Priya: ok, practical items — we'll share two prompt datasets and some sample logs. what's the ideal format?
[06:59] Samir: jsonl with input, expected output, and eval metric is ideal. also include sampling settings.
[07:07] Jamie: recap and next steps — jamie to send security pack and pricing, samir to draft benchmark plan and vllm/TGI compat checklist, priya to upload workloads. target dates in the action items.
[07:19] Lena: sounds good, appreciate the clarity.
[07:22] Diego: thanks all.

(End of recording)

Notes on transcription quality: some names transcribed inconsistently; references to vLLM and TGI occasionally mis-cased. occasional filler words and cut sentences preserved to keep authenticity.
